drug_class: Carbapenem antibiotic combined with a beta-lactamase inhibitor
purpose: This medication is used to treat serious bacterial infections in the urinary tract, including kidney infections. It is specifically used for infections caused by bacteria that are hard to kill with other antibiotics. Doctors often use it when other treatments have not worked or when the bacteria are known to be resistant to common antibiotics.
how_it_works: Meropenem is a powerful antibiotic that works by breaking down the outer wall of bacteria, causing them to fall apart and die. Vaborbactam is a helper ingredient that blocks a defense system some bacteria use to destroy antibiotics. Together, they team up to kill bacteria that would otherwise survive antibiotic treatment on their own.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, diarrhea, nausea, and injection site reactions like redness or swelling. Some people may notice changes in certain lab test results, such as liver enzymes. Let your care team know if you experience any unusual symptoms during treatment.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have ever had a serious allergic reaction to penicillin, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics, as you may also react to this medication. It can rarely cause serious allergic reactions, seizures, or severe diarrhea from a bacteria called C. difficile. Also let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, as the dose may need to be adjusted.
typical_dosing: This medication is given through an IV (directly into a vein) by a nurse or healthcare provider, usually every 8 hours over a 3-hour infusion period. The usual dose for adults is 4 grams per infusion. Treatment typically lasts about 7 to 14 days depending on the infection and how you respond.
